stories.title: Chef preserves Hatay's culinary heritage after devastating earthquake
stories.summary: Chef preserves Hatay's culinary heritage after devastating earthquake
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Chef preserves Hatay's culinary heritage after devastating earthquake. Chef preserves Hatay's culinary heritage after devastating earthquake. Source: Africanews English.
article_sentences: More than three years after the devastating 2023 earthquakes, one chef in Turkey's hardest-hit province is preserving the region's rich culinary traditions through a cookbook inspired by loss, resilience, and community.
Chef and cookbook author Şemse Gökalp says the disaster changed her life and motivated her to use her cooking and social media platforms to help survivors.
"The sixth of February was a turning point for all of us...
I tried to do whatever I could through my own profession.
During those difficult days, I put my activity on social media for it to be of use."
Her book, "Kırık Tabaklar," or "Broken Plates," combines traditional Hatay recipes with the personal stories of people she met while volunteering after the earthquake.
The title carries a deeply personal meaning.
Zübeyde Gökalp Kanat, Şemse Gökalp's Sister-in-law: "After the earthquake, her uncle passed away.
Some time later Şemse said: let this book be called 'Broken Plates,' because during the earthquake we set our tables with whatever we had in our hands.
We ate off those broken plates."
Gökalp says she feared Hatay's world-renowned cuisine might disappear after many renowned chefs were lost in the disaster.
Instead, she witnessed food bringing communities together.

stories.title: Major Russian grain export terminal hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
stories.summary: Grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine are falling as both countries attack each other's shipping facilities and ports.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Major Russian grain export terminal hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack. Grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine are falling as both countries attack each other's shipping facilities and ports. Source: BBC World.
article_sentences: A "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia's port city of Novorossiysk has damaged grain export terminals and hit the last major Russian naval base on the Black Sea.
Three people, including an eight-year-old child, were killed and 24 people were injured in the Wednesday nighttime attack.

Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Ukraine had launched rocket and underwater drones in a "unique operation" to strike the Russian naval base at Novorossiysk, although he did not mention grain terminals being hit.
"The occupying fleet and all the infrastructure that supports it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues," Zelensky said.

Most of Russia's Black Sea fleet is docked in Novorossiysk - one of the largest ports in Russia - after it was forced to vacate its former home base of Sevastopol, in the Russia-occupied Crimean peninsula, which was too exposed to Ukrainian attacks.
A major grain trading company confirmed to Russia's TASS news agency that its terminal had been hit, while another told Reuters and Russian outlet RBK the same.
The Russian agriculture ministry announced on Wednesday that it was working to redirect cargo flows to ports in the Baltic and Caspian Seas as well as land routes.
It did not make any reference to Ukraine's attacks but said it was "taking into account current logistical constraints".
Repeated explosions reportedly rang out over Novorossiysk throughout the night as air defences shot down aerial objects.
An emergency situation was declared in the city on Wednesday, after the barrage of drones struck areas around the port and damaged pipelines, suspending water supply for the city.
Elsewhere in the region a man was killed by drone debris, Regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said.
Several locations in the surrounding Krasnodar region were also struck by "several hundred drones" overnight, Kondratyev added, with dozens of buildings damaged, including homes.
